title: Bioinformatic identification of genes and mechanisms related to acute respiratory distress syndrome and sepsis: A bioinformatic study.
authors: Zhang, Rui; Fu, Yinghua; Long, Fang; Cheng, Qiong
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过生物信息学分析鉴定ARDS与脓毒症共享的缺氧相关基因及调控特征，属于纯转录组表达分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，且未采用AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: We hypothesized that acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and sepsis share hypoxia-related transcriptional signatures that reflect overlapping immunopathogenic mechanisms. This study aimed to identify shared hypoxia-related genes and associated regulatory features using bioinformatic analyses. Gene expression datasets GSE28750 and GSE76293 were analyzed separately after within-dataset normalization. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were defined using |logFC| > 1 and adjusted P < .05. Hypoxia-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, PubMed-curated studies, and molecular signatures database, harmonized by official gene symbols, and intersected with common DEGs from both datasets to identify hypoxia-related DEGs (HRDEGs). Gene ontology enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis, interaction network analysis, immune infiltration analysis, and protein-protein interaction analysis using STRING with a minimum interaction score of 0.400 were subsequently performed. Eleven HRDEGs were identified: capping actin protein, gelsolin-like, CKS2, CLU, FLVCR1, FUNDC1, HPSE, LCN2, MAPK14, PFKFB3, PLAC8, and TDRD9. Gene ontology enrichment suggested involvement in cellular iron ion homeostasis- and iron ion transport-related processes. Gene set enrichment analysisindicated enrichment of hypoxia- and inflammation-related pathways. Under the stricter STRING threshold (score >/= 0.400), the protein-protein interaction network showed a limited but biologically plausible interaction pattern among the HRDEGs. Predicted miRNA, ribonucleic acid-binding protein, transcription factor, drug, and immune infiltration analyses further suggested that these genes may participate in inflammatory and immune regulatory processes relevant to ARDS and sepsis. This bioinformatic study identified shared hypoxia-associated genes in ARDS and sepsis and generated testable hypotheses regarding their possible regulatory and immunologic relevance. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and warrant experimental validation in future studies.
abstract_zh: 我们假设急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）与脓毒症共享与缺氧相关的转录特征，这些特征反映了重叠的免疫病理机制。本研究旨在通过生物信息学分析识别共享的缺氧相关基因及其相关调控特征。基因表达数据集GSE28750和GSE76293在数据集内标准化后分别进行分析。差异表达基因（DEGs）定义为|logFC| > 1且调整后P < .05。缺氧相关基因从GeneCards、PubMed精选研究和分子特征数据库中汇编，通过官方基因符号进行统一，并与两个数据集的共同DEGs取交集，以识别缺氧相关DEGs（HRDEGs）。随后进行了基因本体富集分析、基因集富集分析、相互作用网络分析、免疫浸润分析以及使用STRING（最小相互作用评分为0.400）的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析。共鉴定出11个HRDEGs：capping actin protein, gelsolin-like、CKS2、CLU、FLVCR1、FUNDC1、HPSE、LCN2、MAPK14、PFKFB3、PLAC8和TDRD9。基因本体富集分析提示其涉及细胞铁离子稳态和铁离子转运相关过程。基因集富集分析表明缺氧和炎症相关通路富集。在更严格的STRING阈值（评分≥0.400）下，蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络显示HRDEGs之间存在有限但生物学上合理的相互作用模式。预测的miRNA、核糖核酸结合蛋白、转录因子、药物和免疫浸润分析进一步提示，这些基因可能参与与ARDS和脓毒症相关的炎症和免疫调控过程。本生物信息学研究识别了ARDS和脓毒症中共享的缺氧相关基因，并对其可能的调控和免疫学相关性提出了可检验的假设。这些发现应视为探索性的，并需在未来研究中通过实验验证。
